dialog.body: Utilities billing, this is Priya. How can I help you?
Hi, yeah, so, um, my name's Edson Tavares? I'm calling because I got a notice that my payment bounced, and like, it did not bounce on my end? So I want to know what the status is.
Okay, I can look into that. Can you spell your last name for me, and give me the service address or the account number from the bill?
T-A-V-A-R-E-S. Account number, hold on, I've got the paper bill right here. It's, um, it's ending in 4471? And I'm not giving the address, I mean, the account number should be enough, right?
The account number is usually enough to pull it up. Give me a moment. Okay, I have an Edson Tavares here, homeowner account, water and sewer. Is that the one?
Yeah, totally, that's me.
I do see a payment attempt that was returned by the bank. It shows as a returned item, and the balance is back to what it was before the payment. So right now that bill is still open.
Okay, but that's like, wrong? There was money in that account. I checked. So what does that mean, it just, what, it's sitting there unpaid?
Yes, as it stands the balance is unpaid. What date does your paper bill show? Let's make sure we're looking at the same one.
Um, it says bill date November twenty-fourth, and the due date is, let me see, December nineteenth. So, like, that already passed on Friday.
That matches what I have. The bill dated November twenty-fourth, due December nineteenth. And the return was posted on the twentieth.

Right, see, that's annoying, because I didn't even get told until today. And also, can you, like, re-check the read? The meter reading? Because the usage on this thing looks nuts to me. It's like double what we normally use, and nobody's home half the time.
I can request a re-read. I'll put in the request for the meter to be checked again, and a technician would verify the number on the register. I can note that you're disputing the usage on this bill.
Yes. Please. Do that. Because I'm not paying double for, like, a bad read.
Understood. Let me enter that. Would you like the result by phone? I'd want a callback number on the request.
Sure, it's four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-eight-six.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-eight-six. Got it. The request is in. Is there anything else on the account you want noted?
Well, yeah, so the thing is, I do want to get the original amount paid today anyway, so it doesn't pile up. Can I give you a card right now?
Yes, I can take a card payment over the phone. Go ahead whenever you're ready.
Okay, so it's a Visa. Four, one, two, eight, [pause] um, and then, actually, wait. Actually, let me use the website. Sorry. I'd rather just do it myself, I don't like saying it out loud on the phone.
That's fine, no problem. I haven't entered anything, so nothing was started on my end.

Okay, good. Because honestly I have a deadline tonight. I do books part-time for a couple of small businesses, and I've got to get a bunch of stuff closed out by tonight, so I'm kind of juggling this.
I understand. To be clear, the returned payment is still showing, and the re-read request is on file. When you pay, the balance should reflect it once it posts.
And if the re-read comes back different, then what? Like, I pay the whole thing and then get it back?
If the meter is found to have been misread, the bill would be corrected and any overpayment would be applied as a credit or handled by the office. The technician's finding decides that.
Okay. And is there a late fee because of the bounce? Because that was not my fault.
I see a notation, but I can't tell you what the final amount will be until the account is reviewed after the re-read. I'll flag your note that the bank return was disputed so the reviewer sees it.
Okay. That's, yeah, that's fair, I guess. It's just, ugh, it's a hassle, you know?
I understand. You should hear back about the re-read within a few business days, with the holidays possibly adding a day or two.
Alright. Thanks, Priya. I'll do the website thing now.
You're welcome, Mr. Tavares. Good luck with your deadline.
Thanks. Bye.
